concepts.def: Computer-aided design: producing 2D drawings and 3D models on screen, allowing rapid editing, accurate dimensioning and virtual testing before manufacture.
Computer-aided manufacture: using CAD data to drive machines such as routers, laser cutters and milling machines for accurate, repeatable production.
Computer numerical control: machine tools follow programmed coordinate instructions, often G-code, to cut identical parts with high precision.
Building parts layer by layer from digital models, as in 3D printing, enabling complex geometries and rapid prototyping with little material waste.
A subtractive CAM process using a focused laser beam to cut or engrave sheet materials quickly and with very high accuracy.
Testing a digital prototype on screen, for example simulating stresses or assembly, reducing the cost and number of physical prototypes.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Digital Design & Manufacture — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Digital Design & Manufacture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Digital Design & Manufacture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an additive manufacturing process?
options: 3D printing
Laser cutting
CNC milling
Turning on a lathe

mcqs.q: Which is a key advantage of CAD over manual drawing?
options: Designs can be edited and tested virtually before production
It removes the need for any design skill
It guarantees the product will sell
It makes materials cheaper to buy

mcqs.q: How is a CNC machine controlled?
options: By programmed coordinate instructions such as G-code
By a hand-operated joystick during every cut
By voice commands from the operator
By mechanical cams and gears only

mcqs.q: Is CAD the same as CAM?
options: No — CAD is designing and modelling a product on computer; CAM uses computer-controlled machines to manufacture it. CAD data is often exported to drive CAM machines.
CAD software physically manufactures the product.
CAM is a program used for editing photographs of products.
CNC machines are steered manually with a remote control.

mcqs.q: Is 3D printing additive or subtractive manufacture?
options: CAM is a program used for editing photographs of products.
Additive — material is built up layer by layer from a digital model. Milling and laser cutting are subtractive because they remove material from stock.
3D printing carves the shape out of a solid block of material.
3D printing only works with metals.

mcqs.q: Does a CNC machine design the product itself?
options: No — a CNC machine only follows programmed toolpaths generated by a human via CAD/CAM software; it executes instructions, it does not make design decisions.
CNC machines are steered manually with a remote control.
CAM is a program used for editing photographs of products.
CNC machines automatically decide the best design and make it.

sequence.def: Digital workflow begins with the part modelled on screen
FEA and simulation check the model before anything is cut
Software converts the proven model into machine code (G-code)
Material is clamped and the machine zeroed before cutting
CNC router, mill or laser follows the toolpaths automatically
Output is checked against CAD dimensions, then finished
